_comment: Core harness matrix. Each entry changes exactly one knob from the baseline so a delta is attributable to that knob alone.

baseline.name: baseline
baseline.notes: Everything the harness does for the model, nothing more.

harnesses.name: no-reasoning-hint
harnesses.notes: Same tools, but no instruction to state intent before acting.

harnesses.name: terse-tools
harnesses.notes: One-line tool descriptions instead of full usage guidance.

harnesses.name: minimal-tools
harnesses.notes: Tool names only. Tests whether description quality alone moves scores.

harnesses.name: no-search
harnesses.notes: Grep removed; the model must read files to locate code.

harnesses.name: no-shell
harnesses.notes: Cannot run the tests. Tests whether verification loops matter.

harnesses.name: tight-budget
harnesses.notes: Half the step budget. Measures overhead, not capability.

harnesses.name: loose-budget
harnesses.notes: Double the step budget. Does more room help or just cost more?

harnesses.name: drop-old-output
harnesses.notes: Old tool results elided. Common in production context management.

harnesses.name: no-retry-nudge
harnesses.notes: A text-only turn ends the session instead of being nudged.

harnesses.name: verbose-system
harnesses.system_prompt: You are an expert software engineer. Think carefully about the problem before acting. Read the relevant files, understand the existing conventions, make a minimal and correct change, then verify it by running the tests. Never guess at a file's contents. When you are confident the task is complete and verified, call submit with a short summary.
harnesses.notes: A longer, more opinionated system prompt - what a tuned product harness looks like.
